elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience.
elements.evidence: Added clause IV expressly states that Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience.

elements.element: Customer's termination for convenience requires 30 days' prior notice.
elements.evidence: Added clause IV requires 30 days' prior notice.

elements.element: Customer's termination notice must be written.
elements.evidence: Added clause IV expressly requires written notice.

elements.element: Upon Customer's termination for convenience, Vendor must provide a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees allocable to the period after termination.
elements.evidence: Licensor must refund prepaid fees allocable to the period after the effective termination date, which operatively provides the required pro-rata refund.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.
elements.evidence: The operative language grants Licensor termination only for Licensee breach and does not grant Licensor any termination-for-convenience right during the Initial Period or another committed term.

elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience.
elements.evidence: Added clause IV expressly grants Customer a termination-for-convenience right.

elements.element: Customer termination for convenience requires between 60 and 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The clause requires only 30 days' prior written notice, not notice within the 60–90-day fallback range.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee charged to Customer must not exceed three months' fees.
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee is imposed for Customer's convenience termination; therefore, the applicable fee is zero and does not exceed three months' fees.

elements.element: If Vendor has a termination-for-convenience right, it may take effect only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: The operative language grants Licensor no termination-for-convenience right, so there is no Vendor convenience termination that could take effect before the end of a term.

elements.element: If Vendor has a termination-for-convenience right, it requires 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The operative language grants Licensor no termination-for-convenience right, so the condition triggering this notice requirement is demonstrably absent.

result.reason: The redline cleanly satisfies the preferred position by adding a 30-day written Customer termination-for-convenience right and an equivalent pro-rata refund obligation while granting Licensor no convenience-termination right. It is minimal and does not disturb unrelated commercial terms. Drafting quality is strong, though the numbering and the phrase “for purposes of this clause IV” are potentially confusing because the added paragraph IV sits within Article IV.
